description: We are Tuwaiq Space, a team from Jeddah's technical high school for gifted students, established in partnership with Tuwaiq Academy. Our proposed project, Rahat Relay, will compare open elevation data from Harrat Rahat, the Moon, and Mars to identify a Saudi site for simulating how terrain blocks the line of sight between a rover and its base. Our interests include coding, geospatial analysis, and data visualization. We are not recruiting additional team members at this time.
summary: Rahat Relay uses open elevation data from NASA and USGS to identify where terrain in Saudi Arabia’s Harrat Rahat can reproduce the line-of-sight obstruction a rover could encounter on the Moon or Mars. Across 11 route directions, Al Anahi matched Nobile Rim in five directions at both tested grid resolutions. The Rahat axis sector matched Jezero Crater in one direction. In Al Anahi, a fixed relay reduced the worst blocked stretch from 7.49 km to 4.70 km across six routes held out of relay selection. These results help teams choose where to test rover communications on Earth and where terrain may still block the link.
details:
Study question and method

Rahat Relay addresses one practical question for a terrestrial analog: can the terrain reproduce the obstruction a rover would encounter when trying to reach its base? We compared three sectors in Harrat Rahat with Nobile Rim on the Moon and Jezero Crater on Mars. For each matched route, we measured the share of the route blocked, the longest continuous blocked stretch, and the minimum terrain clearance along the line of sight. We compared results at each dataset’s available resolution and on a common 60 m grid.

Relay placement and validation

We selected a fixed relay location using five route directions and tested it on six other directions from the same base. We also compared it with a relay chosen for a single route. Both approaches chose the same location in Al Anahi. In the Rahat axis sector, the single-route placement performed better on the held-out routes. This gives a field team a reason to validate the placement when the rover’s route changes.

Interactive tool and field checks

The interactive tool uses JavaScript and Three.js to display elevation models, compare routes, and illustrate obstruction and relay placement. The model estimates geometric line of sight. Radio performance and safe access to the proposed station need field verification.
